messages.author: 990b3784138fe4f5
messages.subject: Endemic-epidemic models in RTMB
parts:
Dear TMB users,

to get a better understanding of `RTMB` and what it has to offer, I implemented several endemic-epidemic models in `RTMB`.
This type of model is widely used to model routine surveillance counts of infectious diseases and is already implemented as `hhh4()` in the R package `surveillance`.
I compared parameter estimates, log-likelihoods and runtimes between the individual `RTMB` models and their `hhh4` counterpart.
As I documented the workflow and the differences compared to `hhh4()`, this test somehow turned into a guide on endemic-epidemic models in `RTMB`.
Encouraged by the ease of use and runtime differences, we are now working on re-implementing endemic-epidemic models in `RTMB` in a new R package.

So, if some of you are interested in multivariate count time series models, you could check out the guide here:

https://ee-hub.codeberg.page/hhh4TMB/

I would also really appreciate any feedback, comments, or tips you might have from your experience with TMB/RTMB. I'd be very interested to hear your thoughts on this!

Sophie

it is relatively straight forward to import SPDE type objects via the fmesher package into RTMB. 

Hans

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Endemic-epidemic models in RTMB
parts:
In section '2.5 Simulation' it's mentioned that the `RTMB` simulation function is not working with autoregressive models.

The explanation is simply, that Y[t,] depends on Y[t-1,] but there's no distribution assignment for time t=1.
A simple workaround is to add this statement before the loop (assuming you want zero initialization like the manual version):
if (inherits(Y, "simref")) Y[1,] <- 0
